description: Machine-readable source of truth for EngineOS risk, autonomy, gates, parallelism, retry, router escalation, repair-loop and telemetry policy — nine blocks (risk, autonomy, gates, parallelism, retry, prompt_signals, router, repair, telemetry), added across P1 (risk/autonomy/gates/parallelism/retry) through P7 (telemetry). rules/risk-autonomy.md, rules/gates.md and rules/parallelism.md stay the human-readable mirror and are not edited to match. scripts/validate-engineos.sh checks this file: C16 extracts prose numbers (wave cap, retry attempts/escalations, spec threshold) and enum tables and compares them against this file; C17 checks prompt_signals; C18 checks the router block; C20 checks repair; C22 checks telemetry — so a future prose edit or block change that diverges fails CI.

inputs.low: Trivially undone, e.g. a git revert.
inputs.high: Irreversible, or reversible only with data loss.
Production, other teams, or external consumers.
PII, credentials, financial, or clinical data.
Public/published API, DB schema, or event payload.

levels.permitted: Recommend, draft, or propose a diff — do not apply it.
Apply reversible changes in the working tree.
Apply, but a human gate precedes any external effect.
Bounded autonomous operation, monitored, with a kill switch.

prompt_signals.note: Prompt-classification EREs for kernel.sh scale (were hardcoded in the UserPromptSubmit advisor before the kernel owned them). Countable nouns in scale are plural-only on purpose: 'add a component' is one unit and must not trip fan-out advice. design_weak only counts alongside an action verb.

repair.note: Check-level failure policy: what to do when a validation check is red during a fix loop. The agent-unit counterpart is the retry block; both encode the same bound discipline (rules/parallelism.md: two attempts, one escalation, then a human) over different failure kinds — an agent unit reports an envelope status, a check exits nonzero. Read by scripts/kernel.sh repair; hooks/stop-verify.sh reads the numbers for its block message. The numeric agreement with retry is evidence-based, not law: if P7 telemetry ever justifies a different check bound, this block changes and nothing else does.

telemetry.note: Kernel-decision event capture: which routes, decision rules and verifications actually fired, as ids and outcomes only — never prompt text (value_pattern has no whitespace class; scripts/telemetry.sh rejects on append and validate). Written by hooks/prompt-advisor.sh and hooks/stop-verify.sh to $GITDIR/engineos-telemetry/<session_id>.jsonl in the consumer project, only where .engineos/ exists (the scaffolder's own opt-in gate) and ENGINEOS_TELEMETRY is not 0. Read by skills/retro (step 1) and scripts/usage-report.sh; reaped by hooks/ensure-project-layout.sh after retention_days. Events live in .git and never reach CI — validate-engineos.sh C22 checks this policy and the plumbing, never the data. The samples are asserted by C22b against the running telemetry.sh, the self-validating-registry pattern of routing.json's sample_path and router.fixtures. Attempt-level repair/retry outcomes are deliberately absent: no hook mediates those model-invoked kernel calls, and their designed home is the exec-journal schema, written by the ai-se-os runner follow-on.

router.note: Escalation policy for the P3 router agent: when the deterministic kernel answer is not enough and a model must produce a dispatch plan. Read by scripts/kernel.sh route-escalate; the fixtures are asserted by validate-engineos.sh C18e and scripts/test-kernel.sh.
